title: Why deactivating a user may not end their SP session
desc: Three stages over time. First the user has signed in: the SP has started its own session. Then the user is deactivated at the IdP: none of the sources read says a logout is sent to every SP, which is not verified, so do not rely on it for offboarding. Then the SP session can live on until it expires: the assertion's NotOnOrAfter only bounds when the assertion may be delivered, not how long the SP session lasts, so keep SP sessions short.
